name: Incline push-up
cue: Keep hands on a stable elevated surface; lower your chest toward it while maintaining torso alignment.
setup: Choose a firm counter or securely anchored high surface.
steps: Place hands on the edge and step back until body is straight.
Bend elbows, bringing the chest toward the surface without collapsing through the hips.
Press away and exhale without bouncing.
mistakes: The surface shifts or slides
Use an immovable surface and test it before putting weight on it.
Hips sag during the descent
Raise the incline, shorten the set and gently brace the abdomen.
readiness: Lower the incline only after smooth, repeatable sets.

name: Push-up
cue: Brace the trunk and press through a comfortable, controlled range, without sagging at the hips.
setup: Start in a plank with hands slightly wider than or around shoulder width.
steps: Keep head, torso and legs moving as one unit.
Lower until you reach a comfortable depth, then press through the palms.
Finish without forcing the elbows past a comfortable position.
mistakes: The lower back sinks
Brace the midsection and use an incline until alignment is controlled.
Elbows flare abruptly and shoulders feel crowded
Experiment with hand position and a comfortable elbow path.
readiness: Aim for several technically consistent reps before using harder leverage.

name: Pike push-up
cue: Raise hips and bend elbows to lower the head slightly in front of the hands; press back up with control.
setup: Start in a pike position, hips high and hands planted on a nonslip floor.
steps: Shift a manageable share of weight into the hands.
Bend the arms to lower the head toward a point slightly ahead of the hands.
Press the floor away to return to the pike without a rushed neck movement.
mistakes: Head descends straight between the hands with neck strain
Use a smaller range and position your gaze between hands.
Hips drop and movement becomes a floor push-up
Maintain a pike shape or regress to incline pressing.
readiness: Progress when shoulder comfort and balance are repeatable.

name: Wall handstand hold
cue: Use a clear wall, careful entry and a safe exit; maintain active shoulders during brief controlled holds.
setup: Clear the wall and floor; learn how to return safely to the ground first.
steps: Enter a wall-assisted inversion with a suitable, controlled method.
Press firmly through the hands and keep breathing during a brief hold.
Exit intentionally rather than waiting for fatigue to cause a fall.
mistakes: Kicking up without an exit plan
Use supervised practice or return to pike holds.
Excessive lower-back arching
Reduce hold time and gently align ribs over pelvis.
readiness: Only increase duration if wrist comfort, shoulder control and exit remain reliable.

name: Bodyweight squat
cue: Stand with steady foot contact; sit between the hips to a comfortable depth and rise with control.
setup: Stand at a comfortable stance width with feet planted.
steps: Bend hips and knees together, allowing knees to move naturally with the feet.
Lower only as far as you can control with steady foot contact.
Stand tall without bouncing or forcing the knees.
mistakes: Heels repeatedly lift due to lost balance
Adjust stance and use a higher squat target.
Dropping rapidly into the bottom
Use a controlled speed and reduce range while learning.
readiness: Increase depth or repetitions only while balance and joint comfort remain good.

name: Reverse lunge
cue: Step backward and lower through a comfortable range, then return without losing balance.
setup: Stand tall near a stable support if balance is uncertain.
steps: Step one foot back to a comfortable staggered stance.
Bend both knees and lower vertically as far as you can control.
Push through the front foot to return and switch sides.
mistakes: The back step is too narrow, causing wobbling
Place feet a little wider side-to-side and use a support.
The front knee collapses inward abruptly
Move slowly and find a foot and hip alignment you can control.
readiness: Build reliable balance on both sides before adding range.

name: Glute bridge
cue: Press through planted feet and raise hips using glutes, avoiding excessive lower-back arch.
setup: Lie on your back with knees bent and feet on the floor.
steps: Position feet where you can press evenly through them.
Raise the hips by squeezing the glutes, keeping the ribs controlled.
Lower slowly without dropping the pelvis.
mistakes: Lower back does most of the movement
Reduce height and think of extending at the hips rather than arching.
Feet are so far away that hamstrings cramp
Move feet a little closer and reduce the hold.
readiness: Progress once pelvis remains level and the movement is comfortable.

name: Dead bug
cue: Keep ribs and pelvis controlled as an opposite arm and leg extend slowly.
setup: Lie on your back, arms up and hips and knees bent.
steps: Exhale gently to settle ribs and pelvis into a stable position.
Slowly lower an opposite arm and leg only as far as you can control.
Return, pause and alternate sides while breathing.
mistakes: Lower back arches when the leg extends
Shorten the reach or move the arms and legs separately.
Repetitions become fast and uncontrolled
Use fewer reps with a brief pause on every reach.
readiness: Extend farther only when rib/pelvis control is consistent.

name: Hollow body hold
cue: Brace and only extend arms or legs as far as you can without your lower back arching.
setup: Lie on your back and begin with knees tucked.
steps: Gently tuck the pelvis to limit lower-back arching.
Lift head/shoulders only if comfortable, then extend limbs to a controllable position.
Breathe through a short hold; reset when posture changes.
mistakes: Low back arches as legs lower
Tuck the knees or raise legs higher.
Holding breath to maintain tension
Shorten duration and breathe calmly.
readiness: Increase lever length before chasing long holds.

name: Active hang
cue: Use a secure bar; support some weight with feet as needed while engaging shoulders gently.
setup: Use a properly secured bar with a clear area below.
steps: Hold the bar with feet supported if full body weight is too demanding.
Gently engage the shoulders without aggressively pulling the body upward.
Release under control and return feet to the ground.
mistakes: Dropping straight into a painful passive shoulder position
Use foot support and a smaller comfortable shoulder movement.
Grip fails unexpectedly
Keep feet close to support and reduce duration.
readiness: Increase load or hold time only if shoulders and grip stay comfortable.

name: Assisted pull-up
primary: Latissimus dorsi, upper back, elbow flexors
cue: Use reliable assistance to pull without swinging and lower under control.
setup: Choose stable foot support or reliable assistance under a rated bar.
steps: Start with shoulders engaged and keep the body relatively quiet.
Pull toward the bar while assistance takes part of the load.
Lower slowly and reset with support before fatigue distorts posture.
mistakes: Assistance is unstable or poorly attached
Use a stable foot-assisted method or rated equipment.
Kicking legs to finish reps
Increase assistance until the pull is controlled.
readiness: Reduce assistance when both upward and downward phases are repeatable.

name: Pull-up
primary: Latissimus dorsi, upper back, elbow flexors
cue: From a controlled hang, pull toward the bar without kicking, then lower smoothly.
setup: Use a secure overhead bar with a comfortable grip.
steps: Begin with a controlled hanging shoulder position.
Pull through elbows toward ribs while keeping legs quiet.
Lower under control to a safe finish; avoid a forced dead hang if uncomfortable.
mistakes: Using a pronounced swing to cross the bar
Reduce difficulty with assistance and smaller controlled sets.
Neck cranes excessively to reach chin height
Keep neck neutral and focus on a reproducible range.
readiness: Add repetitions only while the same smooth range is maintained.

name: Dip
cue: Use stable bars and a comfortable range; lower under control and press to support.
setup: Use stable parallel bars, with feet supported if necessary.
steps: Begin in a controlled support hold, with shoulders comfortable.
Bend elbows to lower only to a range your shoulders tolerate.
Press up steadily without bouncing or forcing extra depth.
mistakes: Forcing an unusually deep bottom position
Use less depth or assisted dips and monitor shoulder comfort.
Dropping into the lowering phase
Slow the descent or return to support holds.
readiness: Do not progress to unassisted dips until support and range are controlled.

name: L-sit tuck
cue: On secure parallettes, press through arms and lift bent knees while maintaining trunk tension.
setup: Use securely supported parallettes or suitable bars.
steps: Press into handles and lift shoulders away from them.
Bring bent knees toward chest while keeping trunk active.
Hold briefly with controlled breathing, then lower feet.
mistakes: Shoulders collapse toward ears during hold
Use a shorter hold or toe-assisted support.
Fighting for straight legs too early
Maintain a compact tuck until basic support is reliable.
readiness: Progress by extending one knee at a time while keeping support stable.

name: Pistol squat
cue: Use only a controllable single-leg depth; hold secure support if balance or mobility is limiting.
setup: Use a clear floor and hold secure support if needed.
steps: Balance on one foot and extend the other leg comfortably.
Lower in a controlled single-leg squat only as far as balance allows.
Stand without bouncing or twisting through discomfort.
mistakes: Forcing depth despite heel lifting or wobbling
Use a box target and a support while building range.
Knee or hip pain is ignored
Stop and choose a comfortable supported alternative; seek advice if symptoms persist.
readiness: Choose more depth only after comfortable, repeatable control.

name: Wall push-up
cue: Place hands against a stable wall and lower chest toward it; step closer to reduce load.
setup: Face a solid wall and place hands around chest or shoulder height.
steps: Step back to a distance you can manage.
Bend elbows and bring the chest toward the wall without sagging.
Press away, maintaining steady foot contact.
mistakes: Standing too far away and losing control
Move feet closer and reduce body angle.
Rushing the return by bouncing off the wall
Use a steady pace and softer contact.
readiness: Step farther away or try a safe high incline when ready.

name: Knee push-up
cue: Support knees and hands, keeping shoulders, hips and knees approximately aligned.
setup: Kneel on a comfortable mat and place hands slightly ahead of shoulders.
steps: Align shoulders, hips and knees in a strong line.
Lower chest toward the floor within a comfortable range.
Press up without bending sharply at the waist.
mistakes: Hips stay high while only the head lowers
Move trunk and hips together or use an incline.
Hands move too far forward and shoulders become uncomfortable
Bring hands beneath a workable shoulder line.
readiness: Progress to shorter sets of floor push-ups or lower inclines.

name: Decline push-up
cue: Place feet on a low secure step; press with controlled torso alignment.
setup: Put feet on a low, non-slip, stable step.
steps: Set hands securely on the floor with trunk braced.
Lower chest toward the floor while resisting hip sag.
Press away; dismount carefully from the raised position.
mistakes: Step slides or feet lose contact
Use a lower secure platform or return to floor push-ups.
Lower back arches as fatigue accumulates
Shorten the set and reduce elevation.
readiness: Only increase elevation if current form and shoulder comfort stay reliable.

name: Dip support hold
cue: Support yourself on stable parallel bars with controlled shoulders and elbows.
setup: Place hands on securely mounted parallel bars.
steps: Press up to a supported position with feet ready to assist.
Hold with shoulders stable and breath relaxed.
Come down slowly with the aid of feet when possible.
mistakes: Shrugging or trembling uncontrollably at the top
Use foot support to reduce demand.
Trying long holds despite wrist discomfort
Shorten the holds or choose a different pressing support.
readiness: Add brief controlled dip motion only after support feels stable.

name: Assisted dip
cue: Use foot support and lower only through a comfortable range.
setup: Use stable bars and predictable foot assistance.
steps: Start from a comfortable supported position.
Lower through a modest range while keeping assistance steady.
Press up smoothly, then reset with feet.
mistakes: Assistance disappears at the hardest point
Keep support consistent across the entire repetition.
Shoulders are forced far below elbows
Use a shallower pain-free range.
readiness: Reduce assistance only when all repetitions look alike.

name: Scapular pull-up
cue: From a supported hang, move shoulder blades slightly without bending elbows substantially.
setup: Grip a secure bar with feet supported when needed.
steps: Keep elbows mostly straight while initiating movement from shoulder blades.
Move body a small distance by drawing shoulders down and toward stability.
Relax back to starting position without dropping abruptly.
mistakes: Large arm bend turns the drill into a partial pull-up
Use less effort and think small shoulder movement.
Shoulders are pushed painfully into end range
Shorten range and add foot support.
readiness: Build repeatable small-range scapular control before more demanding hangs.

name: Band-assisted pull-up
primary: Latissimus dorsi, upper back, elbow flexors
cue: Use a securely attached band appropriate for your body weight and pull with control.
setup: Attach a suitable band to a properly rated bar; follow band safety guidance.
steps: Use a stable way to load the assistance without snap-back risk.
Pull smoothly with the band helping the hard part.
Lower under control and safely step out.
mistakes: Band is frayed, misattached or can recoil unexpectedly
Replace the band or use foot-assisted pull-ups.
Bouncing against elastic assistance
Pause briefly and control the lowering phase.
readiness: Transition to a lighter band only after consistent reps.

name: Negative pull-up
primary: Latissimus dorsi, upper back, elbow flexors
cue: Safely reach the top using a stable platform and lower in a slow, supported manner.
setup: Use a secure bar and a stable step to reach the high position.
steps: Start above the bar without jumping into an unstable catch.
Lower with controlled speed through a safe range.
Use the step to return to the start instead of repeated max-effort jumps.
mistakes: Jumping to the top and swinging
Start from a proper platform or use assistance.
Trying to lower so slowly that control collapses
Shorten the time and end the set sooner.
readiness: Lengthen the lowering phase only if you control the whole descent.

name: Chin-up
cue: Use palms-facing grip on a secure bar; pull and lower without swinging.
setup: Use a comfortable palms-toward-you grip on a secure bar.
steps: Start from an appropriate, stable hang.
Pull elbows down as body rises toward the bar.
Lower smoothly without swinging or forcing a painful elbow position.
mistakes: Wrists twist uncomfortably to hold grip
Adjust grip width or use neutral-grip equipment if available.
Kicking the legs to reach the bar
Use assistance and focus on smooth, quiet repetitions.
readiness: Build reliable reps before adding load.

name: Inverted row
cue: With a safely rated bar, keep torso aligned while pulling chest toward the support.
setup: Set a reliably anchored bar at a suitable height.
steps: Hold bar and lean back with feet supported.
Pull chest toward hands while keeping pelvis and ribs aligned.
Lower to straight arms without suddenly dropping the shoulders.
mistakes: Using an unstable bar or non-rated furniture
Choose properly anchored exercise equipment.
Hips sag into an arch
Raise the body angle or shorten the set.
readiness: Walk feet forward only once technique is stable at a higher angle.

name: Ring row
cue: Anchor rings properly, lean backward and pull handles toward your ribs.
setup: Use correctly rated rings and verified anchors.
steps: Lean back with a straight body and feet firmly planted.
Pull rings toward ribs, letting the arms follow a comfortable path.
Lower slowly while preventing straps from swinging.
mistakes: Straps are uneven or anchor is suspect
Check both before loading and stop if uncertain.
Shrugging shoulders up to ears at the top
Reduce angle and aim for a smooth pull.
readiness: Become more horizontal only after repeatable stable reps.

name: Chair squat
cue: Sit gently toward a stable chair and rise without collapsing.
setup: Use a sturdy, unmoving chair behind you.
steps: Stand with feet comfortably apart.
Send hips back and bend knees to gently touch the seat.
Stand up with steady feet without dropping onto the chair.
mistakes: Falling heavily onto the chair
Use a higher seat or support until lowering is controlled.
Rocking far forward before standing
Position feet and trunk for a controlled rise.
readiness: Lower the target or try free squats when reps are easy and stable.

name: Split squat
cue: Keep a stable staggered stance and lower vertically through comfortable range.
setup: Stand with one foot forward and one back at a width that feels stable.
steps: Keep feet in place and lower by bending both knees.
Use a comfortable range and steady upright torso.
Press into the front leg to return, then swap sides.
mistakes: Feet form a tightrope, making balance unreliable
Widen your stance or hold a rail.
Back heel position forces ankle discomfort
Adjust stride length and use a more comfortable depth.
readiness: Progress through range and sets before trying dynamic lunges.

name: Step-up
cue: Stand onto a stable low step without bouncing from the trailing leg.
setup: Choose a low step that cannot tip or slide.
steps: Place a foot fully on the step.
Press through the elevated leg to rise while keeping the pelvis controlled.
Step down slowly instead of hopping.
mistakes: Pushing off strongly from the trailing foot
Use a lower step and focus on leading-leg control.
Step height forces hip hiking
Reduce the height until ascent stays smooth.
readiness: Add height sparingly after balanced reps on both legs.

name: Single-leg glute bridge
cue: Lift hips from one planted foot, keeping pelvis level and movement controlled.
setup: Lie supine with one foot planted and the other leg raised comfortably.
steps: Brace ribs and maintain a level pelvis.
Press through planted foot to lift hips with the glutes.
Lower gently and compare both sides.
mistakes: Pelvis rotates sharply when lifting
Use two-leg bridges until you can control the hips.
Lower back arches to gain height
Use smaller hip extension and a deliberate pause.
readiness: Increase hold time only without pelvis twisting.

name: Calf raise
cue: Rise onto toes slowly, then lower under control with a stable support if needed.
setup: Stand on a stable floor near a fixed support.
steps: Rise onto the balls of the feet without rolling outward.
Pause briefly at a comfortable high point.
Lower heels at a controlled pace.
mistakes: Bouncing rather than controlling the lowering phase
Slow down and reduce repetitions.
Ankles roll outward at the top
Use hand support and a smaller range.
readiness: Try one-leg variations after steady bilateral work.

name: Supported single-leg squat
cue: Hold a secure support while lowering onto one leg to a comfortable height.
setup: Hold a fixed sturdy support and stand on one leg.
steps: Bend the standing hip and knee as you sit toward a safe target.
Use support to control balance and depth rather than to yank upward.
Stand back up with steady foot contact.
mistakes: Support is loose or moves under load
Choose a fixed rail or stable structure.
Standing knee buckles inward as balance is lost
Reduce depth and use more support.
readiness: Gradually use less assistance after controlled repetitions.

name: Bird dog
cue: On hands and knees, extend opposite limbs without rotating the trunk.
setup: Start on hands and knees on a comfortable surface.
steps: Brace gently while keeping pelvis roughly level.
Extend opposite arm and leg without rotating the torso.
Return and alternate sides with a brief controlled pause.
mistakes: Leg raises too high, arching the lower back
Reach long rather than high.
Pelvis rotates during the reach
Shorten the extension and move slowly.
readiness: Increase reach or hold length only after the trunk remains steady.

name: Forearm plank
cue: Brace your trunk while breathing naturally, keeping elbows under shoulders.
setup: Set elbows under shoulders and legs at a manageable distance.
steps: Gently brace ribs toward pelvis and keep breathing.
Hold a steady, comfortable body line.
Finish before hips sag or shoulders lose position.
mistakes: Holding the breath for the full duration
Choose a shorter hold and breathe quietly.
Hips sink as fatigue builds
Switch to knees or shorter sets.
readiness: Build quality time before trying harder leverage.

name: Side plank
cue: Support on one forearm and knee or foot, keeping hips level.
setup: Place one forearm on the floor and stack or bend knees.
steps: Lift the hips to make a stable line from shoulder to hips.
Maintain level breathing while the supporting shoulder remains comfortable.
Lower under control, then repeat on other side.
mistakes: Supporting shoulder feels pinched or unstable
Try a bent-knee version or another lateral-core drill.
Hips rotate toward floor
Shorten the hold and line up shoulders and pelvis.
readiness: Progress from bent knees to straight legs once control is reliable.

name: Bear crawl hold
cue: Hover knees slightly with hands and feet on the floor while keeping trunk steady.
setup: Place hands below shoulders and knees below hips.
steps: Curl toes under and brace gently.
Hover knees a few centimeters above the ground while breathing.
Lower knees before trunk control breaks down.
mistakes: Knees rise too high and back rounds sharply
Use a lower hover and shorter holds.
Shoulders creep toward ears
Push the floor away without locking the neck.
readiness: Progress to small steps only when the hold is stable.

name: Pike hold
cue: Put hands on floor and lift hips, distributing weight carefully through arms.
setup: Place hands on the floor with knees bent if needed.
steps: Lift hips so the torso forms a manageable inverted V.
Gradually shift some weight through the arms.
Step out carefully while keeping balance and breathing.
mistakes: Forcing heels to the floor at the expense of shoulders
Bend knees and focus on stable upper-body support.
Loading wrists too quickly
Reduce angle and duration; prepare gradually.
readiness: Consider a slightly steeper pike or wall preparation after good control.

name: Single-leg balance
cue: Stand steadily on one leg and lightly use a wall for balance as needed.
setup: Stand beside a wall or rail for optional support.
steps: Shift weight onto one foot without twisting.
Lift the other foot slightly and maintain relaxed breathing.
Lower and repeat on the other side.
mistakes: Locking the knee forcefully to feel stable
Keep a comfortable, soft standing-leg position.
Taking support away too early
Use light fingertip contact while balance develops.
readiness: Extend time or gently move arms after stable holds.
